VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center demand was the defining story of our third quarter. In the three months ended September 30, 2026, Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) grew net sales 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. Total backlog rose 13.0% to $918.0 million, giving us strong revenue visibility into fiscal 2027. Company net sales for the quarter were $412.6 million; adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; and adjusted EPS was $0.15. GAAP results for the quarter, including the net loss of $15.6 million, reflect the recall reserve and restructuring charges described below and are reconciled in the KPI tables accompanying this letter.

The quarter therefore ran on two tracks: rapid, structural growth in data-center cooling, and a commercial HVAC market that remains soft. We are managing the second track decisively while we lean into the first.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale awards in the quarter.
- Record data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million (11.8% margin) and adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- Voluntary GV-400 recall executed quickly and transparently under the CPSC Fast Track program, with replacement valves shipping from our Mequon facility since 28 September.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate cost savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** TDC net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from a year ago, driven by sustained hyperscale demand for liquid cooling and the ramp of the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced last quarter. The two new hyperscale awards we won in Q3 extend our pipeline across additional customer deployments, and together they underpin a record $574.2 million of data-center cooling backlog, up 22.0% year over year and up from $538 million at mid-year. Conversion of this backlog spans late fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 as projects reach their installation windows — visibility into future revenue that few industrial companies can match. We are investing ahead of this growth: year-to-date capital expenditures of $41.8 million are weighted toward TDC capacity and test infrastructure, and our supply chain and field teams are organized to convert backlog on schedule. The structural build-out of AI and high-performance computing infrastructure is a multi-year tailwind for our thermal management portfolio, and we are positioned to capture it.

**Building Controls & Valves.** BCV net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, as nonresidential construction activity remained soft and gas-valve shipments were affected by temporary order pauses. During the quarter we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400/GV-410 series combination gas valves sold to OEM customers, in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program — a proactive, customer-first decision made on our own initiative. Our quality team identified the root cause (an out-of-specification diaphragm compound from a supplier lot), completed corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon facility on 28 September. We recorded a $21.6 million reserve in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement, and logistics, and we have lodged a recovery claim against the component supplier. No injuries have been reported. A small number of OEM customers have paused new GV-400 orders pending the public recall notice; those pauses are reflected in our updated guidance, and we are working closely with those customers to resume shipments promptly.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion (previously $1.78–1.84 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million (previously $255–270 million), reflecting continued softness in commercial HVAC end markets, recall-related order pauses, and a more cautious view of the fourth quarter. Behind the update, the trajectory is improving. Project Keystone, our company-wide cost program, is targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027; $6.2 million of restructuring charges were recorded in the quarter as first actions were taken. Our record TDC backlog converts to revenue through fiscal 2027, supporting growth even before commercial HVAC demand recovers. Free cash flow was negative in the quarter, reflecting recall-related outflows, working capital timing, and capacity investment; we expect those pressures to ease as remediation spend rolls off and Keystone savings build.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

Our priorities for the coming quarters are clear: complete the GV-400 remediation with the same speed and care we have shown to date, deliver Keystone savings on schedule, convert our record backlog safely and on time, and work constructively with our lender group on the requested waiver and amendment.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees. Their urgency and care on behalf of customers — most visibly in the recall response — reflect the values of this company, and we are proud of how they responded. We also thank the OEM customers who worked alongside us on the recall; their partnership made a fast remediation possible. Demand for thermal management and fluid control is structurally growing, our backlog is at a record, and we are acting decisively on costs. We are grateful for your continued trust and support.

Dana Whitcombe, President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander, EVP & Chief Financial Officer

- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale awards in the quarter.

**Building Controls & Valves.** BCV net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, as nonresidential construction activity remained soft and gas-valve shipments were affected by temporary order pauses. # Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: VRDF) — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders

**[DRAFT v1 — ticket IR-2026-Q3-014 — for review by D. Whitcombe / M. Ostrander / P. Raman. Not for distribution. Scheduled release: Thursday 5 November 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET; conference call 4:30 p.m. ET.]**

---

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center demand was the defining story of our third quarter. In the three months ended September 30, 2026, Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) grew net sales 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. Total backlog rose 13.0% to $918.0 million, giving us strong revenue visibility into fiscal 2027. Company net sales for the quarter were $412.6 million; adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; and adjusted EPS was $0.15. GAAP results for the quarter, including the net loss of $15.6 million, reflect the recall reserve and restructuring charges described below and are reconciled in the KPI tables accompanying this letter.

The quarter therefore ran on two tracks: rapid, structural growth in data-center cooling, and a commercial HVAC market that remains soft. We are managing the second track decisively while we lean into the first.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale awards in the quarter.
- Record data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million (11.8% margin) and adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- Voluntary GV-400 recall executed quickly and transparently under the CPSC Fast Track program, with replacement valves shipping from our Mequon facility since 28 September.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate cost savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** TDC net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from a year ago, driven by sustained hyperscale demand for liquid cooling and the ramp of the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced last quarter. The two new hyperscale awards we won in Q3 extend our pipeline across additional customer deployments, and together they underpin a record $574.2 million of data-center cooling backlog, up 22.0% year over year and up from $538 million at mid-year. Conversion of this backlog spans late fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 as projects reach their installation windows — visibility into future revenue that few industrial companies can match. We are investing ahead of this growth: year-to-date capital expenditures of $41.8 million are weighted toward TDC capacity and test infrastructure, and our supply chain and field teams are organized to convert backlog on schedule. The structural build-out of AI and high-performance computing infrastructure is a multi-year tailwind for our thermal management portfolio, and we are positioned to capture it.

**Building Controls & Valves.** BCV net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, as nonresidential construction activity remained soft and gas-valve shipments were affected by temporary order pauses. During the quarter we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400/GV-410 series combination gas valves sold to OEM customers, in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program — a proactive, customer-first decision made on our own initiative. Our quality team identified the root cause (an out-of-specification diaphragm compound from a supplier lot), completed corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon facility on 28 September. We recorded a $21.6 million reserve in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement, and logistics, and we have lodged a recovery claim against the component supplier. No injuries have been reported. A small number of OEM customers have paused new GV-400 orders pending the public recall notice; those pauses are reflected in our updated guidance, and we are working closely with those customers to resume shipments promptly.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion (previously $1.78–1.84 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million (previously $255–270 million), reflecting continued softness in commercial HVAC end markets, recall-related order pauses, and a more cautious view of the fourth quarter. Behind the update, the trajectory is improving. Project Keystone, our company-wide cost program, is targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027; $6.2 million of restructuring charges were recorded in the quarter as first actions were taken. Our record TDC backlog converts to revenue through fiscal 2027, supporting growth even before commercial HVAC demand recovers. Free cash flow was negative in the quarter, reflecting recall-related outflows, working capital timing, and capacity investment; we expect those pressures to ease as remediation spend rolls off and Keystone savings build.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

Our priorities for the coming quarters are clear: complete the GV-400 remediation with the same speed and care we have shown to date, deliver Keystone savings on schedule, convert our record backlog safely and on time, and work constructively with our lender group on the requested waiver and amendment.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees. Their urgency and care on behalf of customers — most visibly in the recall response — reflect the values of this company, and we are proud of how they responded. We also thank the OEM customers who worked alongside us on the recall; their partnership made a fast remediation possible. Demand for thermal management and fluid control is structurally growing, our backlog is at a record, and we are acting decisively on costs. We are grateful for your continued trust and support.

Dana Whitcombe, President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander, EVP & Chief Financial Officer

November 5, 2026

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: VRDF) — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders

**[DRAFT v1 — ticket IR-2026-Q3-014 — for review by D. Whitcombe / M. Ostrander / P. Raman. Not for distribution. Scheduled release: Thursday 5 November 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET; conference call 4:30 p.m. ET.]**

---

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center demand was the defining story of our third quarter. In the three months ended September 30, 2026, Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) grew net sales 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. Total backlog rose 13.0% to $918.0 million, giving us strong revenue visibility into fiscal 2027. Company net sales for the quarter were $412.6 million; adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; and adjusted EPS was $0.15. GAAP results for the quarter, including the net loss of $15.6 million, reflect the recall reserve and restructuring charges described below and are reconciled in the KPI tables accompanying this letter.

The quarter therefore ran on two tracks: rapid, structural growth in data-center cooling, and a commercial HVAC market that remains soft. We are managing the second track decisively while we lean into the first.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale awards in the quarter.
- Record data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million (11.8% margin) and adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- Voluntary GV-400 recall executed quickly and transparently under the CPSC Fast Track program, with replacement valves shipping from our Mequon facility since 28 September.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate cost savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** TDC net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from a year ago, driven by sustained hyperscale demand for liquid cooling and the ramp of the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced last quarter. The two new hyperscale awards we won in Q3 extend our pipeline across additional customer deployments, and together they underpin a record $574.2 million of data-center cooling backlog, up 22.0% year over year and up from $538 million at mid-year. Conversion of this backlog spans late fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 as projects reach their installation windows — visibility into future revenue that few industrial companies can match. We are investing ahead of this growth: year-to-date capital expenditures of $41.8 million are weighted toward TDC capacity and test infrastructure, and our supply chain and field teams are organized to convert backlog on schedule. The structural build-out of AI and high-performance computing infrastructure is a multi-year tailwind for our thermal management portfolio, and we are positioned to capture it.

**Building Controls & Valves.** BCV net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, as nonresidential construction activity remained soft and gas-valve shipments were affected by temporary order pauses. During the quarter we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400/GV-410 series combination gas valves sold to OEM customers, in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program — a proactive, customer-first decision made on our own initiative. Our quality team identified the root cause (an out-of-specification diaphragm compound from a supplier lot), completed corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon facility on 28 September. We recorded a $21.6 million reserve in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement, and logistics, and we have lodged a recovery claim against the component supplier. No injuries have been reported. A small number of OEM customers have paused new GV-400 orders pending the public recall notice; those pauses are reflected in our updated guidance, and we are working closely with those customers to resume shipments promptly.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion (previously $1.78–1.84 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million (previously $255–270 million), reflecting continued softness in commercial HVAC end markets, recall-related order pauses, and a more cautious view of the fourth quarter. Behind the update, the trajectory is improving. Project Keystone, our company-wide cost program, is targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027; $6.2 million of restructuring charges were recorded in the quarter as first actions were taken. Our record TDC backlog converts to revenue through fiscal 2027, supporting growth even before commercial HVAC demand recovers. Free cash flow was negative in the quarter, reflecting recall-related outflows, working capital timing, and capacity investment; we expect those pressures to ease as remediation spend rolls off and Keystone savings build.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

Our priorities for the coming quarters are clear: complete the GV-400 remediation with the same speed and care we have shown to date, deliver Keystone savings on schedule, convert our record backlog safely and on time, and work constructively with our lender group on the requested waiver and amendment.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees. Their urgency and care on behalf of customers — most visibly in the recall response — reflect the values of this company, and we are proud of how they responded. We also thank the OEM customers who worked alongside us on the recall; their partnership made a fast remediation possible. Demand for thermal management and fluid control is structurally growing, our backlog is at a record, and we are acting decisively on costs. We are grateful for your continued trust and support.

Dana Whitcombe, President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander, EVP & Chief Financial Officer
